thread:
maria: Heads-up — spotted a regression in staging after the model onboarding merge (PR #824). Median p50 latency for text-generation up ~35% for the same load.
maria: CI perf-run failed on the nightly matrix: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/11345 (perf suite: generation_latency > threshold)
kevin: ugh. which change in #824 could cause this — tokenizer or config drift?
kevin: can you paste the perf summary from the job?
maria: snippet from the job log:
```
Model: model-v2-2026-03
Batch 1: p50 85ms -> 115ms (+35%)
KV cache hit-rate dropped 98% -> 62%
Kernel selected: fallback_matmul_small_batch
```
kevin: KV hit-rate drop flags something — maybe the tokenizer now emits more tokens (longer sequences) -> cache fragmentation
sophie: I ran a quick tokenization diff: new tokenizer adds <|extra_space|> tokens around punctuation for some locales. That increased avg seq len by ~8% on our test prompts.
sophie: But that doesn't fully explain +35% latency. I also saw more frequent fallback kernel selection in the runtime profiling attached to the CI artifact.
ryan: I pulled a flamegraph from the runner VM. TL;DR: inference runtime spends ~40% more time in matmul kernels; kernel selector is preferring the safe path for shapes due to changed sequence-length distribution.
ryan: profiler command I used:
```
./tools/profiler --run ci/artifacts/11345 --metric kernel-time --group-by kernel,shape
```
ryan: Output (truncated):
```
fast_matmul_fp16 (shape 128x64) : 12ms
fallback_matmul_small_batch (shape 1x1024) : 78ms (+140%)
kv_cache_lookup : 4ms (but calls increased x3)
```
maria: Reproduced locally with model-v2 checkpoint + the new tokenizer config. Batching heuristics now see more single-token interactions, so batch formation favors small batches -> poor kernel choice.
kevin: Could be two simultaneous effects: longer sequences causing more KV churn + more single-request tails preventing batching. Both nudge kernel selector toward smaller-shape slower kernels.
kevin: We should bisect whether it's the checkpoint, tokenizer config, or runtime change. Who owns the merge? @sophie for tokenizer, @ryan for runtime followups? 
ryan: I can bisect runtime commits quickly. Suggest baseline with model-v1 + new tokenizer, model-v2 + old tokenizer, etc.
sophie: I'll run tokenization-only job across the perf harness today and share token length diffs.
ci-bot: perf-run started: build/11346 (matrix: tokenization-only, model-v1/model-v2 combinations) — https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/11346
maria: If we can't find a quick mitigation, we should hold the rollout. Ops, can we hold the staged rollout? @ops-bot
ops-bot: rollback-plan: canary deploy paused. Revert PR option available. To proceed with immediate revert comment `/revert 824`.
kevin: Let's hold. Meanwhile try a hotfix: in kernel-selector, prefer fast_matmul_fp16 for shapes matching our expected runtimes even if batch smaller, at least for the canary.
ryan: quick patch tested: tweak selector threshold -> reduces p50 by ~20% in local repro. I'll open a PR for selector tweak + unit tests: #845
sophie: token diffs posted in the CI job artifacts. model-v2 introduces a tokenizer config flag `preserve_whitespace=true` that is expanding token counts in some locales.
sophie: if we flip that flag only for on-device conversion (don't expose to hosted), token lengths go back to baseline in the harness.
maria: plan: 1) pause rollout, 2) revert model-v2 in canary while we bisect (if revert approved), 3) land selector tweak as short-term perf mitigation, 4) followup to reconcile tokenizer config and update onboarding docs.
kevin: sounds good. Who will submit the revert? maria? ryans? (also add release notes about the rollback)
maria: I'll hit revert now for canary and notify product. `/revert 824 --scope canary`
ci-bot: revert job queued: build/11347 — running smoke + perf sanity.
ryan: opened selector tweak PR #845 and linked to this thread. Running CI perf on it now.
maria: thanks everyone. Keep thread updates short — post results from CI perf and bisect jobs here. :thumbsup:
